header.name: emet
header.tagline: A witness that reports what it found, and decides nothing.

flows.title: How bytes become a verdict that claims no authority
flows.alt: Eight stages of a witness run: subject, anchor, read paths, recompute, compare, markers, lattice, chain. The raw-byte hash is pinned out of band, so it does not travel inside the file it describes. The same bytes are hashed through channels that share no code, and one channel alone is an inability rather than agreement. Embedded authority claims are reported by offset and never obeyed. Every verdict token is checked against a closed set before it is emitted, and the set excludes TRUSTED by construction. Three outcomes: match, drift, and unverifiable.
flows.footnote: Nothing here loops back. The lane reports what it found, and decides nothing.

stages.title: Subject
stages.note: The bytes as they are, before anything presents them.

stages.title: Anchor
stages.note: The raw-byte hash is pinned outside the file it describes.

stages.title: Read paths
stages.note: One file, hashed through channels that share no code.

stages.title: Recompute
stages.note: The digest is derived again from the bytes on disk now.

stages.title: Compare
stages.note: Recorded against re-derived, and a view against its source.

stages.title: Markers
stages.note: Embedded claims are reported by offset, and never obeyed.

stages.title: Lattice
stages.note: A token outside the closed set raises before it is printed.

stages.title: Chain
stages.note: The run appends a row that hashes the row before it.

outcomes.label: MATCH
outcomes.note: the recorded digest and the bytes agree

outcomes.label: DRIFT
outcomes.note: a confirmed difference, and it outranks doubt

outcomes.label: UNVERIFIABLE
outcomes.note: an inability to check, never a silent pass

flows.kicker: one verdict, handed to a stranger
flows.title: How a verdict travels to someone who shares no state with you
flows.alt: Eight stages of a receipt: envelope, subjects, identity, canonical form, address, signature, re-derive, verdict. The receipt's identifier is a hash of the receipt with its own identifier, signature, and per-implementation block removed, so a doctored field changes the address it is stored under. An optional signature covers that same body, so the two never disagree about what they cover. A reader on another machine recomputes the address and compares, with no anchor store, no log, and no network. Three outcomes: valid, tampered, and unverifiable, and tampered outranks unverifiable.
flows.footnote: A signed receipt with no key to check it reads unverifiable. It never reads valid.

stages.title: Envelope
stages.note: One completed verdict, in the canonical JSON form.

stages.title: Subjects
stages.note: Each path, with the digest that was actually recorded.

stages.title: Identity
stages.note: The tool's own artifact hash, naming what produced this.

stages.title: Canonical
stages.note: One byte form, so two machines compose the same bytes.

stages.title: Address
stages.note: A hash of the receipt with its own id and signature cut.

stages.title: Signature
stages.note: Optional, over that same body, so the two agree on scope.

stages.title: Re-derive
stages.note: The reader recomputes it. No store, no log, no network.

stages.title: Verdict
stages.note: Tampered outranks unverifiable, as it does upstream.

returns.label: THE STORED ID IS NEVER TRUSTED, ONLY RECOMPUTED

outcomes.label: RECEIPT VALID
outcomes.note: the address re-derives from the bytes present

outcomes.label: RECEIPT TAMPERED
outcomes.note: a doctored field or a changed subject

outcomes.label: RECEIPT UNVERIFIABLE
outcomes.note: malformed, or a subject that cannot be read

cards.title: Every word emet may say, and nothing else
cards.alt: The nine channels of emet's closed verdict lattice, one to a row, with what each channel judges and the exact tokens it may emit. The primary lattice judges an anchored path re-read now and emits MATCH, DRIFT, or UNVERIFIABLE. Coherence judges a rendered view against the source bytes and emits COHERENT, VIEW_DIFFERS_FROM_SOURCE, or UNVERIFIABLE. Corroboration judges two read paths for one file and emits CORROBORATED, QUARANTINE_READ_PATH_DIVERGENCE, or UNVERIFIABLE. Audit judges the append-only chain of records and emits INTACT or BROKEN. The receipt channel judges a portable receipt offline and emits RECEIPT_VALID, RECEIPT_TAMPERED, or RECEIPT_UNVERIFIABLE. The monitor judges one watched file as MATCH, DRIFT, or MISSING, and the baseline it read from as INTACT or CHANGED. Perception judges a path between two observations as UNCHANGED, DRIFTED, NEW, or GONE. The revert channel judges whether a clean revert path exists and emits REVERTIBLE or NOT_REVERTIBLE. No channel admits a word that asserts authority.
cards.footnote: No count and no digest is drawn here. What is drawn is the shape of the set: nine channels, each one closed, and a union that contains no word asserting authority. The repository's own test holds every row against the frozen set in emet/verdict.py, so a token added to the code and not to the drawing fails the build, and so does a token drawn here that no channel will emit.

fields.note: MATCH / DRIFT / UNVERIFIABLE. Absence of drift is a match or an inability to check, and never trust.

fields.value: a view against the source bytes
fields.note: COHERENT / VIEW_DIFFERS_FROM_SOURCE / UNVERIFIABLE. What you are shown, held against what is on disk.

fields.value: two read paths for one file
fields.note: CORROBORATED / QUARANTINE_READ_PATH_DIVERGENCE / UNVERIFIABLE. Paths that disagree are quarantined, not resolved.
INTACT / BROKEN. The chain re-links end to end, or it names the record it broke at.
RECEIPT_VALID / RECEIPT_TAMPERED / RECEIPT_UNVERIFIABLE. Valid is a re-derivation, and not a release.
MATCH / DRIFT / MISSING. A file gone from the sweep is reported, never quietly skipped.
INTACT / CHANGED. The baseline is checked before anything is checked against it.
UNCHANGED / DRIFTED / NEW / GONE. A path that appeared is news, and so is one that left.
REVERTIBLE / NOT_REVERTIBLE. A fact about the version history, and not permission to act.
